subject: Urgent: VPC inference errors and latency after quantized model rollout

Subject: Re: rollout: quantized-v2 on private cluster - spikes and 503s

Vanessa —

We pushed the quantized-v2 bundle to our private cluster at ~08:30 PT and since ~08:45 we've seen intermittent 5xxs and p95 latency jumping from ~180ms to 3.2-4.8s for text-generation routes. Error pages show 503s from the inference svc; we also see a sustained increase in CPU on the proxy and frequent KV cache evictions.

Attached is a small slice of logs + the deploy manifest. Can the Redwood team advise immediate mitigations — customers on our side are seeing failed predictions in production.

Thanks,
Miguel
Ops Lead, CatalystHealth

I’m really sorry you’re seeing this after the rollout. I’ve looped in Marcus (runtime) and Priyom (CS) to triage immediately. Quick asks while we start a deeper dive:

On Thu, Jul 4, 2028 at 09:26 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marcus, can you start the kernel/metric sweep and confirm whether this looks like KV cache thrashing vs. a quantization incompatibility?

We pulled the logs Miguel attached and started live telemetry. Preliminary findings:
- p95 spikes correlate with large multi-turn chat requests (seq len > 1k) that trigger cache churn.
- The quantized-v2 path introduces a different attention kernel which increases per-token memory working set; combined with CatalystHealth's smaller cache allocation we see repeated eviction and regen of KV pages. That regen is manifesting as increased proxy CPU and occasional 503s when requests block on cache warmup.
- No kernel panics or OOMs on the GPU; GPUs show elevated memcpy stalls on the quantized execution path.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered):
A) Temporarily rollback to quantized-v1 (fastest, safe).
B) If rollback is not acceptable, increase the model pool KV cache allocation + bump GPU pool from 4xA10g to 6xA10g for 1 hour to absorb the working set.
C) Tune the runtime to bypass the new attention kernel for chat routes (can be done but is a 3–4 hour engineering change).

I’ll push a diagnostic bundle to S3 and open CH-3472 with traces and a reproduction harness.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: RE: rollout: quantized-v2 on private cluster - spikes and 503s

Miguel / CatalystHealth leadership —

TL;DR: After the quantized-v2 rollout we observed a new attention kernel that expands the runtime working set for multi-turn chat. With CatalystHealth’s current KV cache allocation the runtime experienced cache churn resulting in increased token latencies and intermittent 503s while the cache warmed.

Immediate actions taken (done within the day):
- We coordinated a safe rollback to quantized-v1 at 12:05 PT; this restored p95 latency to baseline within ~10 minutes and eliminated 503s.
- Marcus pushed a diagnostic bundle and we opened Jira ticket CH-3472 with traces and reproduction steps. See link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CH-3472
- Temporary capacity increase was on standby but not required after the rollback.

Next steps (short term):
- Engineering will deliver a runtime patch to make the quantized-v2 attention kernel opt-in for chat routes (ETA: 48 hours).
- CS/Dev will propose a KV cache sizing recommendation for CatalystHealth (we’ll share an empirical sizing table).
- We’ll schedule a technical postmortem + tuning workshop with CatalystHealth engineering next week.

We apologize for the impact and appreciate the fast coordination. I’ll follow up with the PM/engineering postmortem and a proposed mitigation timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
